chapter: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
title: Rehearsals and free orchestrations from publishers
summary: Mutt rehearsed new numbers from complimentary publisher orchestrations given to working bands, while smaller groups bought lead sheets.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let me just ask you a couple of more questions about Mutt, and then we'll pass on -- because we'll get back to Mutt later when you worked with him with Ory, naturally. But you said he was the leader of the band, absolutely.
Did he rehearse the band, or did he just...
Yes, when we got a new piece of sheet music, or they had... Music publishers would send out complimentary orchestras. So all bandleaders would...they would send them out. You didn't have to even
What was the purpose of that?

Well, for you to play the particular arrangements for that particular tune. They didn't do it with every tune. Some of them you would buy, buy the lead sheet, and there was always somebody in the band who could copy.
I would guess (correct me if I'm wrong) the ones that were up and coming pieces they sent you free, so they'd get you to play it, and then everybody else would buy it that heard you play it.
But the ones that were established didn't need to send free copies, because you'd have to buy them anyway.

Yes, that's right. I didn't explain myself right. They gave it to the band that was playing on certain jobs, where they know people would hear it. And like you said, the other small groups, not well known, would buy them.
